subject: math

objective.text: Make an inch ruler and use it to measure lengths.

explanations.title: Make an inch ruler
explanations.text: Lay an inch tile at the left end of the strip. Draw a line where it ends. Write 1 above the line. Keep moving the tile with no gaps. Write each number above its mark.

explanations.title: What 0 means
explanations.text: Write 0 at the left edge. It means you have not measured anything yet. It is where you start to measure.

explanations.title: What each number means
explanations.text: Each number tells how many inches you have measured so far. The number 1 is one length unit. The end of a 2 inch paper clip is at the number 2.

explanations.title: A foot
explanations.text: The last number on the ruler is 12. 12 inches make a larger unit called a foot. 12 inches equals 1 foot.

explanations.title: Units inside units
explanations.text: A foot is made of 12 inches. A ten is made of 10 ones. A hundred is made of 10 tens. A dollar is made of 100 cents.

explanations.title: Why use a ruler
explanations.text: A ruler keeps all the inches together. You can measure all at once. This is faster than moving one tile again and again.

explanations.title: Unit size and number
explanations.text: The smaller the length unit, the more of them you need. The larger the length unit, the fewer you need.

explanations.title: Add inches to make a foot
explanations.text: To add 9 inches and 6 inches, make a foot first. 9 needs 3 more to make 12. Then 3 are left over. So you get 1 foot 3 inches.

examples.title: A 2 inch paper clip
examples.text: Lay the paper clip along the ruler from 0. It ends at 2. The paper clip is 2 inches long. A line drawn from 0 to 2 is the same length.

examples.title: A 5 inch index card
examples.text: The index card ends at 5 on the ruler. It is 5 inches long. 5 inches plus 7 inches equals 12 inches, or 1 foot.

examples.title: Edwin and Tina's truck
examples.text: Edwin measures with toothpicks and gets 4. Tina measures with lima beans and gets 12. A bean is a smaller unit, so she needs more of them. Both are right.
